strings.name: Wang Tao
strings.summary: Wang Tao, also known as Frank Wang, founded DJI, turning flight-control research into civilian drones and imaging products. Its teams developed the Phantom, Inspire and Mavic series, expanding access to aerial imaging. He shared the 2019 IEEE Robotics and Automation Award with his mentor Li Zexiang.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Products are company-team achievements. Launch, reporting and award dates are distinguished; interview views are attributed to media reports. Birth retained to year only.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded DJI, advancing civilian drone products, flight-control technology and imaging applications, with influence on global consumer and industrial drone markets.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: HKUST BEng in 2006 and MPhil in Electronic and Computer Engineering in 2011.
strings.facts.f2.label: Academic mentor
strings.facts.f2.value: Robotics scholar Li Zexiang supervised his MPhil research and supported early drone development.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Flight control and aerial imaging
strings.highlights.h1.text: With teams, integrated flight control, gimbals and imaging into products, helping drones evolve from hobbyist assemblies into more accessible devices.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Engineering research and entrepreneurship
strings.highlights.h2.text: Began designing drones while studying at HKUST, then founded DJI; mentors and engineering teams also supported the technical development.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Management interview reported
strings.timeline.t1.text: IT Home reported the next day that LatePost published an interview discussing staff mobility, incentives and organizational changes.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Inaugural Distinguished Engineering Alumni Award
strings.timeline.t2.text: One of three inaugural HKUST School of Engineering recipients, recognized for professional achievement and global impact.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Shares IEEE award with Li Zexiang
strings.timeline.t3.text: The pair receive the IEEE Robotics and Automation Award for contributions to civilian drones, aerial imaging and related engineering entrepreneurship.
strings.timeline.t4.title: DJI introduces Mavic Pro
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company unveils a portable drone with folding arms and a stabilized 4K camera; Wang discusses its design philosophy in the announcement.
strings.timeline.t5.title: DJI launches Inspire 1
strings.timeline.t5.text: The company introduces a drone with a 4K camera and wireless HD video transmission in San Francisco.
strings.timeline.t6.title: DJI introduces the original Phantom
strings.timeline.t6.text: The company launches a pre-tuned multirotor aircraft that can carry a GoPro or other lightweight camera.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earns MPhil
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completes a postgraduate degree in Electronic and Computer Engineering at HKUST, following his 2006 BEng.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds DJI
strings.timeline.t8.text: Turns drone research at HKUST into a startup, gradually developing a Shenzhen-based drone company.
